title: Bluehaven Analytics — Integration onramp: SDKs, gateway, rate-limits
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-09 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Solutions), Marco (Bluehaven CTO), Jenna (Bluehaven Eng Manager), Omar (Bluehaven SRE), Sofia (Bluehaven DS)

Summary: quick discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main asks: SDK support (python/node), LangChain & LlamaIndex connectors, gateway vs sidecar proxy tradeoffs, per-tenant rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks to Datadog/Prometheus. They flagged procurement/VPC peering and SOC2/KMS as gating items.

Topics: SDKs, LangChain, LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy, quotas, observability, security

Action items (captured in notes below)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex: Alright thanks everyone for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We invited Priya who'll cover the technical piece and Liam on solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Marco: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to talk about the onramp. We want to understand integration effort more than pricing right now.
[00:13] Jenna: Yeah engineering wants a clear path to plug Redwood into our stack — we run a mix of microservices and a small Kubernetes cluster in GCP, and we also have one on-prem customer environment.
[00:22] Priya: Great, that helps. Quick qualifier questions: are you evaluating Hosted, Dedicated, or Private first? Or all three?
[00:28] Marco: All three — preferred is Hosted for dev/test, Dedicated for production if latency/cost predictable, and Private for the on-prem customer. But procurement will require clear controls for Private.
[00:39] Omar: On the SRE side, key constraints: VPC peering with our VPCs, egress firewall rules, and KMS integration are musts. Also we need per-tenant quotas to prevent noisy neighbors.
[00:50] Alex: Understood. Priya, maybe run through SDKs and integration options.
[00:53] Priya: Sure. Redwood offers official SDKs for Python and Node, plus a thin REST API. SDKs include streaming helpers, retry/backoff, and native support for function calling. For LangChain and LlamaIndex, we have connectors and examples — some community contribs for llamaindex that map to our client. Note: names in the examples sometimes say "RedwoodInfer" in older snippets, the repo has been updated but the auto-transcript may show older names.
[01:18] Jenna: How frictionless is the LangChain adapter? We use LangChain orchestration in prod for retrieval-augmented generation.
[01:23] Priya: There are two patterns: direct SDK adapter where your agents call Redwood via the client (we provide a LangChain LLM wrapper), and a gateway pattern where you run a proxy/sidecar that translates internal LLM calls to Redwood endpoints and handles auth/rate-limits locally. The wrapper is easiest to get started. The gateway gives you more control over observability and routing.
[01:40] Sofia: For LlamaIndex, any gotchas? We use LlamaIndex for embeddings pipelines and chunking.
[01:46] Priya: Works fine. We provide an embeddings endpoint compatible with the typical LlamaIndex interface. Watch out for embedding dimensionality mismatches when you move between models; we map dims in the connector but you should pin model versions in your index config.
[01:58] Marco: On the gateway vs sidecar: what's the latency tradeoff? We care about sub-150ms p50 for short prompts.
[02:05] Priya: Gateway adds an extra network hop but enables request batching and local caching (prefix/KV cache). For p50 short prompts, we usually see a 10-30ms added depending on infra. The benefit is consistent per-tenant quotas and ability to route to dedicated pools. Sidecar in-process is lowest latency but more ops.
[02:23] Omar: Does the gateway handle token accounting and per-route quotas? We need to throttle customers at different tiers.
[02:29] Priya: Yes, gateway or Redwood's control plane can enforce per-api-key and per-route quotas. You can set soft and hard limits, burst windows, and token-based billing hooks. We also expose headers in responses with token usage so you can do local metering.
[02:43] Jenna: Observability — we use Datadog and Prometheus. Can we ship traces/logs to those?
[02:48] Priya: Absolutely. Redwood Console emits trace IDs and spans for requests; we have a Datadog integration and can forward metrics to Prometheus via a scrape endpoint in Dedicated/Private. Token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency histograms, and per-route error rates are available. For Hosted, logs are accessible from the Console, and you can set up forwarding.
[03:08] Alex: Wanted to call out model fallbacks — if a Dedicated pool reaches capacity, you can configure automatic fallback to a compatible Hosted variant to prevent outages. Useful for predictable availability.
[03:18] Marco: That fallback is interesting. Any way to pin versions for compliance? We need tamper-proof version pins for some regulated customers.
[03:24] Priya: Yes, version pinning is supported across deployments. Private customers can also bring their own model binary if needed for air-gapped setups.
[03:33] Omar: For Private, what's included in the on-prem package? We have strict egress rules so need a control plane pattern.
[03:39] Priya: Private offers a customer-managed control plane with optional telemetry proxy. We support HSM/KMS integrations, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. For air-gapped installs we ship an installer and an offline package; this typically adds 4-6 weeks ops work.
[03:55] Jenna: Can you walk through a sample flow for a request from our app to Redwood via the gateway?
[04:00] Priya: Sure. App -> internal API -> gateway sidecar (does auth, rate-limit, local cache check) -> if not cached batch to Redwood endpoint -> JWKS signed token to Redwood -> Redwood runtime serves from dedicated pool (or hosted) -> tokens billed and response returned. Gateway emits spans that link to Redwood traces.
[04:21] Marco: Any constraints on model sizes or quantization profiles for Dedicated? We might want to run q4_0 or q8_0 profiles to reduce cost.
[04:28] Priya: Dedicated pools support popular quantizations; runtime will pick kernels accordingly. We'll share recommended quant profiles based on your sequence patterns.
[04:36] Alex: Quick procurement note: some customers ask for SOC2 + ISO docs and a pen-test report. We can share those in the security pack.
[04:42] Marco: Yes please, security pack and an architecture diagram of the Private control plane.
[04:46] Priya: Noted.
[04:48] [05:00] Speaker 2 (automated): --- 00:05:00 check-in ---
[05:05] Jenna: On quotas again, is there built-in support for per-tenant billing reports or do we export tokens and compute cost ourselves?
[05:12] Priya: We provide per-api-key usage exports (CSV/JSON), and the Console has billing breakdowns by token, model, and route. For Dedicated we can integrate with your internal billing via webhooks.
[05:24] Omar: For rate limits we need both per-second TPS limits and monthly token caps. Are both supported?
[05:30] Priya: Yes, you can combine short-term TPS limits with long-term token caps and set different actions for breach (reject, queue, degrade to smaller model).
[05:40] Sofia: Degrade to smaller model — curious how quality regressions are handled. Do you provide eval tooling?
[05:45] Priya: Redwood Optimize includes eval suites you can tie to prompt sets. You can set regression alerts and run canary rollouts with automatic fallbacks. We'll set up a sample eval run during the pilot.
[05:55] Marco: Timeline — how long to get a pilot running? We have a small internal team to run tests.
[06:01] Alex: For Hosted dev/test you can be up in hours. For a Dedicated pilot with capacity and routing, estimate 2–4 weeks. For Private on-prem, 6–8 weeks depending on network approvals and procurement.
[06:13] Jenna: Any client-side changes needed for LangChain agents? We prefer not to leak secrets into the index.
[06:18] Priya: Use the gateway to centralize keys and token exchange. The LangChain wrapper supports token refresh flows and doesn't require long-lived keys in code.
[06:26] Marco: Are there example repos for our stack? We're on Python 3.11 and Node 18.
[06:31] Priya: Yes, we'll share a GitHub sample that shows LangChain, LlamaIndex, and a gateway sidecar example with GKE. Note: some older samples reference older endpoints; we'll point you to the updated branch.
[06:43] Omar: Security question: what encryption-at-rest options exist for Dedicated? Do you support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys)?
[06:50] Priya: For Dedicated and Private we support CMEK via KMS providers and HSM integrations for key lifecycle. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and can discuss dedicated key options for enterprise customers.
[06:59] Marco: Competitors in our eval are Anthropic (hosted), an in-house Llama stack, and an OEM from a larger cloud vendor. How do you compare on cost predictability?
[07:10] Alex: Redwood focuses on serving economics — transparent token pricing, toolkits to reduce per-token costs (batching, cache), and Dedicated contracts for commit pricing. We can run a benchmark to show comparative unit costs.
[07:22] Jenna: Would like a benchmark simulating our mix: 60% short prompts, 30% multi-turn chat, 10% embeddings.
[07:29] Alex: Sounds good. We'll propose a benchmark plan in the next step.
[07:33] [07:40] Marco: Compliance: need SOC2 attestation + audit log forwarding for regulators.
[07:45] Priya: We'll include SOC2 and an audit log export mechanism. For Private we can stream audit logs to your SIEM directly.
[07:56] Sofia: Small question on embeddings: do you support batch embeddings and async jobs?
[08:00] Priya: Yes, batch embeddings and async endpoints for large index builds are supported. We also expose per-request embedding dims in the response.
[08:11] Alex: Let's talk next steps and owners.
[08:14] Priya: Proposed pilot: 2-week hosted dev test using LangChain wrapper + gateway PoC (sidecar) to validate quotas and observability. Then Dedicated pilot (~4 weeks) with capacity if results are good. Private on-prem can be scoped in parallel.
[08:28] Marco: That timeline works. Procurement will need the pricing sheet and security docs.
[08:33] Alex: We'll send a pilot proposal, benchmark plan, and security pack. Also a sample repo.
[08:40] Jenna: Can we kick off next Wednesday for the hosted smoke test?
[08:44] Alex: Yes, we'll aim to start Wed 2027-06-16.
[08:47] Omar: I'll need a network diagram to take to infra for VPC peering approvals.
[08:52] Priya: I'll attach a reference architecture with gateway patterns (sidecar vs external proxy).
[08:58] [09:00] Speaker 1: --- 00:09:00 closing notes ---
[09:05] Marco: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[09:07] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts.
